memos.headline: Momentum bifurcation: S09 and S07 lead while S08 and S06 break down into oversold territory
memos.body: I see a clear split in this universe today. S09 is at its 52-week high with RSI 73.8 and +12.8% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks—this is the strongest trend in the group, though the overbought reading warrants tight trailing stops near 128. S07 and S05 remain in powerful uptrends, trading well above their 200-day means (+37.1% and +42.6% respectively) with only shallow drawdowns from highs, though S05's +77.2% 26-week return and +42.6% premium to the 200d make me cautious about chasing. On the weak side, S08 at RSI 22.3 and -8.1% below its 50d is deeply oversold and breaking down—I'd need a reclaim of the 50d average (roughly 270) to turn constructive. S04 is the weakest on a 12-week and 26-week basis, trading below both moving averages with -12.9% relative strength over 12 weeks, and I see no reason to step in front of that trend.

views.note: At 52-week highs with dominant relative strength (+12.8% vs SPY over 4w); would reassess on a break below 128 (~5% trailing stop).
Strong uptrend with +18.3% 12w relative strength and only -3.4% drawdown; a close below 590 (50d area) would change my view.
Massive momentum with +77.2% 26w return and near highs, but extreme extension above 200d (+42.6%) limits confidence; would trim on a break below 310.
Quiet relative outperformer with +4.8% 12w rel strength, above both averages, RSI 54.9—steady trend with low drawdown of -5.8%; invalidated below 225.
RSI 22.3 is deeply oversold but the trend is clearly broken at -8.1% below 50d and -13.3% from highs; need a reclaim above ~270 to reconsider.
RSI 34.1 with -8.8% 4w relative strength and -11% drawdown signals distribution; would need a close above 315 (50d area) to turn neutral.

Recent 4w bounce (+4.9%) is encouraging but still below 200d mean (-2.7%) and -14.8% from highs; need a sustained move above 155 to get constructive.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Durable Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between names with expanding margins and accelerating earnings versus those suffering margin erosion despite top-line growth. S10 stands out with 62.5% YoY revenue growth, a 56.0% net margin, and only $8.47B in total debt — the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 also impresses at $102.35B revenue (+15.9% YoY) with a 34.2% net margin and net income up 33.0%, on a modest $14.79B debt load. On the other end, S02 grew revenue 12.2% YoY to $113.16B but saw net income collapse 61.2% to just $2.35B (2.1% margin), signaling severe cost or impairment issues I cannot look past. S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (-5.2%) and shrinking earnings (-12.3%), and its 8.8% margin leaves little cushion — I would need to see a top-line inflection before getting constructive.

views.note: 62.5% revenue growth, 56% net margin, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt — the strongest earnings momentum and balance sheet in the universe.
Revenue +15.9% YoY with 34.2% net margin and net income +33.0%, supported by low $14.79B debt; durable high-quality compounder.
Revenue +18.4% YoY to $77.67B with 35.7% net margin and manageable $43.21B debt, though net income growth of 12.5% lagging revenue growth warrants monitoring.
Largest revenue base at $180.17B with solid 13.4% growth and 38.2% earnings growth, but 11.8% net margin and $55.10B debt limit upside conviction.

Steady 21.2% margin and 20% earnings growth, but only 3.0% revenue growth on a $22.39B base suggests limited top-line catalysts.
31.0% net margin is attractive but $427.20B total debt dwarfs the universe; earnings growth of 11.6% is adequate but leverage risk dominates.

Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and only 8.8% margin — no earnings power floor visible yet.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a 2.1% margin despite 12.2% revenue growth — severe cash-flow compression I cannot underwrite.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky CPI and Rising Long Rates Argue for Quality over Duration
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime—the upper bound is 3.75%, down 75bp over 12 months and 50bp over the last three months—but the pace of cuts is likely to slow given December CPI running at +2.7% YoY with a 0.6% three-month gain that annualizes above 2.4%. Unemployment at 4.40% is flat over three months but up 30bp YoY, signaling a softening labor market that keeps the Fed biased to ease but not urgently. The 10y yield at 4.24% has risen 23bp over three months even as the front end fell, steepening the 10y-2y spread to +65bp—this bear-steepening pressures long-duration growth names while benefiting banks' net interest margins. My regime call is 'late-easing / mild slowdown': favor banks and defensive staples, stay neutral on cyclicals, and be cautious on pure duration-sensitive growth. A CPI print re-accelerating above 3% YoY or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to revisit this framework.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped and steepening curve (10y-2y +65bp, up 34bp YoY) alongside still-easing policy supporting credit demand.
Staples offer defensive positioning in a mild-slowdown regime with unemployment drifting higher and CPI still moderate enough to protect real margins.
Duration-sensitive growth faces headwinds from the 23bp rise in 10y yields over three months despite front-end easing; upside limited until long rates stabilize.
Cyclicals are caught between supportive rate cuts and a softening labor market; I lack conviction until employment data clarifies direction.
Energy faces demand risk from a mild slowdown signaled by rising unemployment, and the easing cycle historically compresses commodity pricing power.
With the curve steepening and policy still easing, rate-sensitive financials/REITs in this bucket should see improving funding conditions.

memos.headline: S01 Earnings Beat Lifts Tone; S06 Negative Narrative Deepens After -4.2% Drop and Continued Churn
memos.body: I see the clearest sentiment divergence between S01 and S06 right now. S01 reported Q2 results on 1/22 with a +2.6% price reaction, accompanied by an Reg FD disclosure the same day—this is a positive tone inflection after a quiet period and suggests the narrative is turning constructive. S06, by contrast, posted a -4.2% move on its 1/13 results, followed by yet another director departure and an 'Other Events' filing on 1/22; the clustering of negative catalysts signals a deteriorating sentiment trajectory that likely has further to run. S08 and S07 each show director-level turnover filings but no financial catalysts, leaving me with low conviction on direction. S09 and S02 had early-January Reg FD disclosures with no observable price reaction data, so I treat those as noise for now.

views.note: Positive earnings reaction (+2.6%) and paired Reg FD disclosure mark a constructive tone shift that may not yet be fully priced.
Clustering of a -4.2% earnings reaction, director departure, and Other Events filing within 10 days signals a deepening negative narrative.
Two director-change filings in quick succession but no financial catalyst—insufficient signal to form a directional view.
Bylaws amendment and director change filed 1/6 are governance noise absent any financial disclosure or price data.
Reg FD disclosure on 1/7 with no price reaction data available; treating as low-information event.
Single Reg FD filing on 1/12 with no accompanying price data—no actionable sentiment signal.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Doubles in One Month While Credit Markets Shrug — Watch for Sanctions or Export-Control Escalation
memos.body: I am flagging a stark divergence: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has nearly doubled over the past month to 474.48, yet HY OAS has tightened 24 bp over the same window and VIX sits at a moderate 15.64. This pattern historically precedes either a rapid policy resolution (bullish) or a delayed credit repricing if the uncertainty crystallizes into concrete sanctions, export controls, or tariff actions. WTI at $59.24 is essentially flat over three months, suggesting energy-supply disruption risk is not yet priced in despite the policy noise. Multiple names in the universe (S01, S02, S06, S09) have filed Reg FD disclosures in January, which could reflect pre-positioning around anticipated policy shifts. My conviction is low across the board because the uncertainty spike lacks a clear catalyst in the evidence I have, but I would change my view materially if new export controls targeting China or energy-sector sanctions are announced.

views.note: Two 8-K filings in ten days (Reg FD and Other Events) suggest active disclosure posture, but without content detail I cannot determine geopolitical exposure direction.
Back-to-back Reg FD filings in January may signal guidance updates tied to policy shifts, but no concrete geopolitical risk is identifiable from filings alone.
Early-January Reg FD disclosure is noted; with policy uncertainty near 475 but credit spreads tight, I see no clear directional geopolitical signal yet.
Single early-January Reg FD filing and no additional data make it impossible to assess geopolitical exposure with any conviction.
With no company-specific filings and the policy uncertainty index doubling, names lacking disclosure transparency carry elevated tail risk from potential sanctions or export-control actions.
No 8-K filings in the evidence set amid a near-100% surge in policy uncertainty suggests limited visibility into how this name navigates potential geopolitical shocks.
